based_on: For 2026, staff propose an average budgetary tax rate increase of 0.57 percent.
This budgetary tax increase includes a 0.70 percent rise for residential and industrial properties, and a 0.35 percent rise for multi-residential and commercial properties.
Staff also recommend an extra tax rate increase for the City Building Fund Levy to pay for transit and housing capital projects.
The recommended 2026 tax rates are subject to the 2026 Mayor's Proposed Budget being adopted as the City's 2026 Budget.
An average residential property assessed at $692,140 will have a municipal property tax bill of $4,252 for 2026, not including provincial education taxes.
Provincial education property tax rates will not change in 2026, so the average household will see no increase in their education tax.
Combining municipal and education taxes, the average household in Toronto will see a total property tax increase of $92, or 1.75%.
Staff recommend keeping the 10% cap on tax increases for commercial, industrial, and multi-residential properties where the increase is more than $500.
Staff recommend raising the maximum household income eligibility limit to $62,000 for property tax, water, and solid waste relief programs starting January 1, 2026.
Proposed user fee changes, not including automatic inflation increases, will bring in $15.14 million in extra revenue.

A 3.75 percent rate increase for solid waste management and rate increases of 3.75 percent for Block 1 and 1.25 percent for Block 2 water and wastewater are expected to bring in $14.13 million for Solid Waste Management Services and $55.15 million for Toronto Water.
Staff recommend suspending the Net Income Share Agreement with the Toronto Parking Authority starting January 1, 2026, so all of its net revenues go to the City while a review takes place.
Staff recommend asking the Toronto Parking Authority Board to consider an inflation adjustment or changed parking rates for 2026.
Staff recommend requiring Solid Waste Management Services to send all future waste collection schedules in a separate mailing.
Staff recommend transferring the $332.996 million balance of the Scarborough Transit Reserve Fund to the City Building Reserve Fund while keeping the money for its intended uses.
Staff recommend authorizing an agreement with Park People with up to $120,000 in matched City funding to support community-led park groups until December 31, 2026.
Subject to Council approval and funding, the expanded air conditioner program would provide up to 1,000 air conditioners before the summer of 2026.
Staff recommend asking the Executive Director of Transit Expansion to study grade separation, underground, or at-grade options for the Eglinton East Rapid Transit project and report back in 2026.
Staff recommend directing the City Manager to review homelessness outreach programs to improve service coordination and long-term housing solutions.
Staff recommend allowing the General Manager of Fleet Services to donate up to five generators at no cost to Kyiv City State Administration in Ukraine for humanitarian needs.

Staff recommend authorizing the transfer of $100,000 to the Angel Foundation for Learning and $700,000 to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success to expand the Student Nutrition Program to eligible new school communities.

Staff recommend authorizing the City Manager and Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer to divide a $75.0 million spending reduction target across City divisions while keeping the overall City Budget the same.
